Robust starting values for the cellGLoc soft corner

Source: R/cellgloc_utils.R
dot-gloc_start_robust.Rd

Until 7.4.0 the soft corner started from a classical fit: every observed cell at weight 1 and \(B\) by ordinary least squares. A redescending weight function started there can settle on a masked solution. This start fits each continuous column on the categorical design alone, along robustbase::lmrob's M-S path: an L1 regression (robustbase::lmrob.lar) followed by an M-step with the bisquare at the L1 fit's residual scale (method = "lM"). The predictors are dummies, which cannot carry a contaminated continuous cell, so casewise robustness is exactly what is needed: a contaminated cell is an outlying response. The starting flags are then those of cellWise::cellMCD on the residuals \(X - U B\), at .gloc_start_alpha. (Corrected: this page first called the fit "MM regression". There is no S step on this path, so it is not the MM estimator.)

.gloc_start_robust(
  X,
  U,
  M,
  alpha = .gloc_start_alpha,
  have_cw = requireNamespace("cellWise", quietly = TRUE),
  control = NULL,
  warn_design = TRUE,
  U_main = U,
  patterns = NULL,
  fit_rows = NULL
)

Arguments

X

\(n x p\) numeric matrix of continuous variables, may contain NA.

U

\(n x q\) design matrix from .gloc_design.

M

\(n x p\) logical missingness mask.

alpha

minimum fraction of unflagged cells per column for cellWise::cellMCD; see .gloc_start_alpha.

have_cw

whether cellWise is available.

control

an robustbase::lmrob.control list; NULL uses the defaults. An empty seed (the default) is replaced by .gloc_start_seed. Its method is set to "lM" for the L1-started fit and left as given for the S-started fallback.

warn_design

whether to warn here about a design that is rank deficient on a column's observed rows. imputeCellGLoc passes FALSE: its mean step (.gloc_update_B) warns about the same design once, and says what the returned fit does.

U_main

the main-effects version of U (see .gloc_update_B); the default, U itself, stands for a design without interaction terms.

patterns

the level combinations; see .gloc_update_B.

fit_rows

optional logical vector over the rows: the per-column fits use only these rows, while the residuals flagged afterwards cover every row. imputeCellGLoc passes the rows without a missing categorical cell when categorical = "em".

Value

a list with B (\(q x p\)), W (\(n x p\), 0 or 1, 0 on missing cells) and S, the scatter cellWise::cellMCD returned for the residuals (\(p x p\)), or NULL when the flags did not come from cellMCD. The categorical EM takes the penalty of its two-start selection from S; see .gloc_lambda.

Details

The path is exactly what robustbase::lmrob(..., init = "M-S") does for a design with no continuous predictor: its coefficients agreed to 0 over 960 column fits. lmrob's default S-estimator start is not used first because it does not converge on many purely categorical designs ("S refinements did not converge in k.max steps", "initial estim. 'init' not converged"): in the 7.4.1 pilot some column failed in 42 of 90 fits with design = ~ ., as often at \(\epsilon = 0\) as under contamination, and on 960 column fits of 200 rows on four factors it failed 54 times, where the L1 start converged every time. The two agree in accuracy (median fitted-mean error against the truth 0.243 and 0.237) and the L1 start needs no subsampling. The S start remains the fallback when the L1-started fit does not converge.

Each response is centred by its median before the fit, because lmrob's stopping rules are relative to the size of the coefficients, and the median is put back through the design: into the intercept column when the design has one, which leaves every other coefficient bit for bit as fitted, and otherwise as the coefficients that reproduce the constant on the observed rows. (Corrected: it used to be added to the first design column, assumed to be the intercept. With design = ~ f - 1 that column is a level's dummy, and the start's fitted means came out 10.25, 0.37 and 10.16 against a truth of 10, 20 and 30, after which the fit flagged 210 cells, 172 of them clean, without a warning.)

A design that is rank deficient on a column's observed rows, an aliased factor say, is fitted on its non-aliased columns as chosen by qr()'s pivoting, and the aliased columns get coefficient 0. (Corrected: this used to surface as "robustbase::lmrob did not converge", naming the symptom.) Level combinations that no observed row identifies are then filled by the rule of the mean step (.gloc_update_B): towards the column median, or, under a design with interaction terms, towards the robust main-effects start wherever that identifies the combination. (Corrected: the first 7.4.1 fix filled design columns one at a time, which missed a never-observed reference level under treatment coding and divided by zero under sum contrasts.)

Every degraded path warns, once per reason, naming the columns: too few observed rows for the design (fewer than \(2q\), or a non-constant design column with fewer than three observed rows), a rank-deficient design, an lmrob error, or lmrob not converging from either start. The first and the last two fall back to the column median as the fitted mean, without group effects. Without cellWise, or if cellMCD fails, a cell is flagged when \(|r_{ij}| / \mathrm{MAD}(r_{.j})\) exceeds \(\sqrt{\chi^2_{1,0.99}}\). What cellMCD prints when it refuses is captured, so a failure is reported once, as a warning, and not also as six lines on the console.
